translation_notes: `from pyshacl.consts import RDFS, SH, RDF_type, SH_property` mixes two kinds of binding: RDFS and SH are Namespace objects (project-owned, pyshacl/consts.py:8-11: `RDFS = Namespace(RDFS_PFX)`, `SH = Namespace(SH_PFX)`) -- the exact ns_import_project idiom -- while RDF_type and SH_property (consts.py:63,76: `RDF_type = RDF.type`, `SH_property = SH.property`) are already-derived URIRef terms, not namespaces, so they cannot become prefixes; they travel as ordinary Python names on both sides, unchanged.

pyshacl.consts is a plain rdflib-based .py module (not written in ldpy), so it exports no `__namespaces__` and `from pyshacl.consts import rdfs:, sh:` cannot resolve directly. Since consts.py is pySHACL's OWN namespace module (project-owned, same reasoning as the LexMalta/recipes ns_rdfa precedent in this stratum), pyshacl_consts_context.py reproduces its RDF/RDFS/SH bindings verbatim plus the `__namespaces__` export the transpiler needs; both original.py and translated.ldpy import from this shim so both sides use identical values.

Anti-hollow-green finding: the generic module-state driver (entry=None) pairs values ONLY by shared Python variable name between the two module namespaces. A prefix import captures no Python name (`rdfs:`/`sh:` are lexical, not runtime bindings), so the generic comparison silently never looks at RDFS/SH at all -- it only ever compared RDF_type/SH_property, which happened to travel as plain names. Verified by sabotage: rebinding `rdfs:` to a wrong IRI via an extra `@prefix rdfs: <...>.` in translated.ldpy left the generic check green. driver.py now also asserts the module's `__namespaces__` table (which every ldpy module exports, ldpy/transpiler/core.py PRELUDE) against the real RDFS/SH values; re-running the same sabotage now FAILs as it should.

classification minor-restructuring: the import line is expressible, but as a split between `from … import p:` (RDFS, SH) and unchanged plain names (RDF_type, SH_property) plus a project-context shim, not a 1:1 rewrite of the single import statement.
